youtube.baslik: Why do low sounds mask high sounds more? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: The traveling wave always moves from the base of the cochlea toward the apex; a low sound passes through the high-frequency regions before reaching its own place and vibrates them too. So a low sound masks a high sound much more strongly than the reverse; this is called upward spread of masking.

cumleler: Why do low sounds mask high sounds more?
The traveling wave always moves from the cochlear base toward the apex.
A low sound passes high-frequency regions first and vibrates them too.
After its peak, the wave dies out quickly, not spreading lower.
So low masks high far more strongly than high masks low.
Low noises like air conditioning cover the high consonants of speech.
